title: Recursive Conditional and Mapped Types knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a mapped type?
options: To map a URL to a server without configuration.
To convert TypeScript to a database schema automatically.
To transform properties by iterating over keys of an existing type.
To loop over object properties at runtime.
questions.answer_key: To transform properties by iterating over keys of an existing type.
questions.explanation: Mapped types derive related type shapes and can modify property names or modifiers.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Recursive Conditional and Mapped Types”?
options: The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with recursive type definitions and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with recursive type definitions and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Recursive type definitions”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Recursive Conditional and Mapped Types”?
options: Check deep transformation utilities, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume recursion depth and compiler limitations is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
questions.answer_key: Check deep transformation utilities, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Deep transformation utilities”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
